description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase the efficiency, coverage, and sustainability of water supply and sanitation services in Paraguay by (a) improving the governance of the sector, (b) improving water services and increasing access to sewerage services in the Asuncion metropolitan area, and (c) increasing access to sustainable water and sanitation services in rural areas.

The development objective of the Water and Sanitation Sector Modernization Project for Paraguay is to increase the efficiency, coverage, and sustainability of water supply and sanitation (WSS) services in Paraguay by: (a) improving the governance of the sector; (b) improving water services and increasing access to sewerage services in the Asuncion metropolitan area; and (c) increasing access to sustainable water and sanitation services in rural areas. There are three components to the project. The first component of the project is support to the modernization of sector governance and institutional strengthening. The component includes support for: (a) the Ministry of Public Works and Communications (MOPC) to strengthen the recently created Water and Sewerage Services Unit; (b) strengthening the Regulatory Entity (ERSSAN) to effectively regulate the sector; and (c) the Environmental Secretariat (SEAM) by strengthening the water resources and the environmental licensing directorates. The second component of the project is urban WSS and institutional strengthening of the Sanitary Services Company of Paraguay (ESSAP). This component includes: (a) institutional strengthening and corporate governance of ESSAP; and (b) priority WSS infrastructure investments. The third component of the project is rural water supply, sanitation, and hygiene education and institutional strengthening of the National Environmental Sanitation Service (SENASA). This component includes: (a) strengthening the SENASA and its governance; (b) increasing coverage of WSS for indigenous communities; (c) increasing coverage of WSS, and hygiene education in rural communities; and (d) construction and/or expansion of services in rural communities using minimum subsidy schemes.

comment.narrative:
<p>Achievement rate is 144 percent of the original target and 119 percent of the revised target. Project beneficiaries are: (a) 440,000 in the urban area of Asuncion, benefited from a improved sanitation environment; (b) 29,000 in the urban area of Asuncion, benefited from a improved sanitation service; (c) 50,000 in the urban area of Asuncion, benefited from an improved water service (network rehabilitation); (d) 12,500 in the rural area of eastern Paraguay, benefited from improved water sources; (e) 6,500 in the indigenous communities in rural areas of Chaco, benefiting from improved sanitation (latrines); (f) 5,500 in the indigenous communities in rural areas of Chaco, benefiting from improved water sources.</p>
<p>In order to avoid double counting, the total project beneficiaries was estimated using (a), (d), and (f), for a total of 458,000 beneficiaries.</p>

title.narrative: Number of new systems providing access to sustainable water supply services to rural communities

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 42 percent of the original target and 100 percent of the revised target. These systems correspond to those in Eastern Paraguay, which were finalized in the early years of the Project. The target was revised due to available financing.</p>

title.narrative: Number of installed latrines for indigenous communities

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 255 percent of the original target and 149 percent of the revised target. About 6,500 indigenous people have benefited from sanitation solutions under the Project.</p>

title.narrative: Kilometers of sewerage collectors rehabilitated from the sewerage system of Asuncion

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 280 percent of the original target and 58 percent of the revised one. During the prioritization of these works some of the resources intended towards sewer rehabilitation contributed to the rehabilitation of 57 kilometers of secondary distribution water networks, benefiting 50,000 people, which partly explains the underachievement of this indicator.</p>

title.narrative: Number of new systems providing access to water supply services to indigenous communities

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 100 percent. 30 systems are finalized. One more system is under construction in the San Jose community, and will be finalized by SENASA once the climatic conditions allow it.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of water connections with working micrometers (less than five years of installation)

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 160 percent. 105,242 micrometers were installed.</p>

title.narrative: Timely availability of ESSAP's external auditing of financial and performance data published through an annual report in ESSAP's website

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. As of Project closing ESSAP is still publishing these documents on their website. They can be found in http://www.essap.com.py/proyectos/informes-de-auditoria/</p>

title.narrative: Characterization of Service Providers (Service Provider Mapping) developed and published in ERSSAN's homepage

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. As of Project closing, the characterization is finalized but has not been made public yet.</p>
<p>Achieved. The Board of Directors counts with two vice-presidents or advisors and one syndicate.</p>

title.narrative: Water and Sewerage Services Unit within the MOPC staffed and equipped, defining the policies for the sector

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The WSS unit has been staffed and equipped, and was elevated to the level of Direction as DAPSAN in 2010. In this role, DAPSAN published the first National Water Plan, setting policies and objectives for the sector.</p>
<p>Achieved. The concession contract between ESSAP and MOPC was signed and served as the basis for the elaboration of a performance-based contract.</p>

title.narrative: Information Management System developed and generating reports for managerial decisions

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. This information system helped ESSAP integrate their various sources of information on works and performance indicators.</p>

title.narrative: Procurement unit strengthened and publishing procurement plans in SEPA

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. Though SEPA no longer exists, SENASA's procurement unit was strengthened and has published its procurement plans throughout implementation.</p>

title.narrative: SIAPS developed and generating reports according to the "Conceptual Framework for the SIAPS"

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved.</p>

title.narrative: People provided with access to "improved sanitation services" under the project in urban areas

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 290 percent. These beneficiaries correspond to the people who benefited from the 28,557 m of sewerage collectors rehabilitated under the Project.</p>

title.narrative: People provided with improved sanitation environment in urban areas

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 147 percent. With the sewerage works realized under the Project, namely the new sewerage collectors  in the Itay Basin (29,798 m) and the rehabilitated sewerage collectors in the Itay and Bella Vista basins, it is estimated that the entire population in both basins have been provided with an improved sanitation environment. Based on ESSAP's cadaster, this corresponds to 440,865 people.</p>

title.narrative: Indigenous people provided with access to "improved sanitation facilities" under the project in rural areas

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 108 percent. These beneficiaries correspond to the people provided with sanitation systems (improved pit latrines) in the Chaco region.</p>

title.narrative: Number of families resettled as per the RAP

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 100 percent. All families were resettled as of the closing date. 15 families chose resettlement outside of the Project area; 24 families chose cash compensation; and 94 families chose a home in the collective resettlement site built at a safe distance from the planned WWTP area.</p>

title.narrative: Number of people in rural areas provided with access to Improved Water Sources under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 100 percent. The beneficiaries are calculated as the sum of beneficiaries from the water systems in the eastern area of Paraguay (12,500 people) and those in indigenous communities in the Chaco region (5,500 people).</p>

title.narrative: Reduction of non-revenue water in the Gran Asuncion Aera

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement rate is 228 percent. The planned reduction by 5 percentage points was surpassed to achieve a reduction of 11.4 percentage points. The NRW activities have been institutionalized through the NRW management unit.</p>
